causalModel.founding: The Long road from Archon to Gideon crosses Middle Argonia. The road follows the firm ground that is available. Here the firm ground is a strip between two meres. The strip lies barely higher than the water.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The neck is the only dry line between the meres for a long way. About 55 m of the neck lies under water. Walkers wade that stretch. The water is up to the waist where it is deepest.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The neck has no residents. Travellers drove poles into both verges. The poles let a walker keep to the causeway when the water covers it.
causalModel.pressures: The water rises over the neck every wet season. The poles rot or fall. A walker who steps off the causeway then is in deep water.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: The meres could dry back. The poles would then stand on dry ground. The travellers would stop replacing the poles.

districts.notes: The stretch of the Long road across the neck between two meres, with its poled wade and the marks at each end.

why.what: The district is the Long road across the neck between two meres. The road wades about 55 m, marked by poles on both verges. A cairn stands at each end.
why.whyHere: The neck is the only firm line between the meres. It lies barely above the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The road runs on south-east toward Archon. It runs on north-west toward Gideon. A marsh track leaves the road at the north-west bend.
why.playerPurpose: The neck is the way across the meres. A walker who keeps between the poles finds the water shallow.
why.microGeography: The neck is a low strip of mud and reed. A deep mere lies to the east. A marsh pond lies to the west.

parcels.orientationWhy: The cairn stands on the dry verge where the road goes down into the water. The poles run on from the cairn along both verges.

why.what: The parcel is the south-east head of the wade. A stone cairn stands on the last dry ground. The first poles of the line stand along both verges.
why.whyHere: The road leaves dry ground here. It goes into the water here.
why.whySpot: The parcel lies on the verge beside the road. It lies just short of the water's edge.
why.whyNeighbours: The drying fire lies a few paces back up the road. The west head lies about 55 m away across the water.
why.playerPurpose: The cairn shows the walker where the wade starts. It also shows which way the causeway runs under the water.
why.microGeography: The ground is the last firm mud before the water. Reeds grow on both sides.

why.whyHere: The spot is the first flat dry ground after the water for walkers who come from Gideon.
why.whySpot: The ring sits on the flat a few paces off the road. The flat lies above the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The south-east cairn lies just down the road. The first poles also lie just down the road.
why.playerPurpose: The ring is a place to stop and dry off after the wade. It lies a few paces from the south-east cairn.
why.microGeography: The ring sits on a dry flat of trodden mud. The flat lies above the mere.

A step of trodden ground links the road to the cairn. The cairn stands at the north-west head of the wade.

approaches.sequence: A walker comes north-west along the road from Archon. Open water lies on both sides of the road. A cairn stands where the road goes into the water. Two lines of poles cross the water from the cairn.
approaches.wayfinding: A walker keeps between the poles to reach the cairn on the far side.

approaches.sequence: A walker comes south along the road from Gideon. A cairn marks the bend where a marsh track leaves the road. Past the cairn the road runs down into the water between two lines of poles.
approaches.wayfinding: A walker goes round the bend and past the cairn. The walker then wades between the poles.

networkTerminals.why: The road from Archon reaches the south-east end of the neck.
The road from Gideon reaches the north-west bend of the neck.

combatSpaces.why: The combat space is the wade between the cairns. Open water lies on both sides. Footing exists only on the causeway.

candidates.why: The Long road crosses a neck between two meres, crossing.major.030 and crossing.major.033. About 55 m of the road lies under 0.1 to 1.3 m of water. No place owns the neck. The ground of the nearest place, the Open Mouth, lies 66 m away.
The Long road crosses water at crossing.major.029. That crossing lies further toward Archon.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The crossing lies 93 m from the centre of Nine-Trunks. The crossing lies inside the ground of the village of Nine-Trunks. Nine-Trunks builds the crossing.
